 Bangladesh's 100th Test ton underlines progress in Test cricket
 Published : 17 November 2026
 • 
 Updated : 17 November 2026, 13:52
 • 
 CRICKET
 SHARE 
 Star Sports Desk 
 Litton Das raises his bat after reaching his century in Johannesburg on Monday which was Bangladesh's 100th century in Test cricket. Photo: AFP 
 Bangladesh had to wait 18 years to reach their first 50 centuries in Test cricket, but the next 50 came in less than half that time.  
 Litton Das brought up the landmark 100th century for the country against South Africa in Johannesburg on Monday, marking another significant step in Bangladesh’s progress in the longest format.
 Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source 
 The milestone came on November 16, exactly eight years and five days after Mominul Haque scored Bangladesh’s 50th Test century against Zimbabwe in Mirpur on November 11, 2018.
 It all started with Aminul Islam on November 11, 2000 as the former captain had become Bangladesh’s first Test centurion, scoring a hundred against India in the country’s inaugural Test. Aminul was only the third batter in history to score a century in his country’s first Test match.
 Read more Whenever Bangladesh are in trouble, I want to handle it: Litton 
 Bangladesh have now become the ninth country to reach 100 Test centuries, achieving the feat in their 165th match. England were the first to do so, in their 162nd Test, against Australia in Brisbane in 1928, when Patsy Hendren scored their 100th century.
 Bangladesh’s progress has been particularly notable over the last decade. Their first 50 centuries came across 110 Tests, while the next 50 required only 55 matches.
 Of the 100 centuries, 15 came between 2000 and 2009, when Bangladesh played 61 Tests. The following decade brought 42 hundreds from 56 matches. Since 2020, Bangladesh have scored 43 centuries in 48 Tests, taking their overall tally to 100.
 Read more Tales from a Test like no other 
 The team have recorded nine centuries in a calendar year on three occasions: in 2014, 2025 and 2026. Another century during the ongoing South Africa tour would set a new national record.
 A total of 29 Bangladesh batters have scored Test centuries among the 112 players who have represented the country in 165 matches. 
 Mushfiqur Rahim leads the country's century-makers with 14 hundreds in 108 Tests, followed by Mominul with 13 in 83 matches. Tamim Iqbal has 10 in 70 Tests, while Najmul Hossain Shanto has nine in 48. Litton's Johannesburg hundred took his tally to eight in 60 Tests, putting him among the country's top five Test centurions.
